evals.prompt: Create a B1 speaking lesson about social media addiction for my teenage student Maria. This is lesson 8 in our course - previous lessons covered: 1) buying time phrases, 2) describing photos, 3) giving opinions, 4) storytelling, 5) active listening, 6) comparisons, 7) giving reasons. She's preparing for an FCE exam but needs to improve her fluency.
evals.expected_output: HTML lesson file saved to gitsite folder
assertions: The lesson includes a Recall Zone that retrieves items from previous lessons (lessons 1-7)
The Recall Zone uses optimal spacing intervals (e.g., recalls from lessons 2, 4, 6 - not just the most recent)
The lesson clearly states the student should produce 70%+ of the content
The lesson includes dual coding (visuals + text) for all new content
The lesson uses interleaving (mixes different practice types)
The lesson includes an 'I can...' self-assessment statement at the end
The lesson opens with retrieval practice BEFORE presenting new content
All feedback targets task/process, not self (no 'Good job!' without specifics)
The file is saved to the gitsite folder with a clear naming convention

evals.prompt: I need a grammar lesson on present perfect vs past simple for my A2 adult student John. He's a professional who needs English for work. This is lesson 12 in our sequence - we've covered basic tenses, modals, and some time expressions in previous lessons. Make it relevant to his business context.
evals.expected_output: HTML lesson file saved to gitsite folder
assertions: The lesson includes a Recall Zone that retrieves grammar points from earlier lessons
The spacing follows research-backed intervals (+3, +7, +14 lessons)
The lesson uses small chunks (max 2-3 new items before practice)
The lesson includes guided practice sequence: I do → We do → You do
The lesson includes interleaved practice mixing present perfect and past simple
The lesson requires the student to explain the rule in their own words (elaboration)
The lesson ends with retrieval + metacognition ('What helped you remember?')
The lesson includes dual coding (visual timelines + text explanations)
The student produces 70%+ of the lesson content

evals.prompt: Build me lesson 15 in my Speaking Pathway course (B1 level). This is a review lesson that should spiral back through lessons 6-14. The focus should be on consolidating the speaking skills we've covered: active listening, comparisons, giving reasons, self-correction, cause & effect, follow-up questions, describing experiences, and expressing preferences.
evals.expected_output: HTML lesson file saved to gitsite folder
assertions: The lesson is explicitly structured as a review/spiral lesson
The Recall Zone retrieves items from lessons 6-14 using optimal spacing
The lesson includes items from multiple previous lessons (not just the most recent)
The lesson follows the Speaking Pathway template principles (even if tab structure varies)
The lesson prioritizes spoken output over written output
The lesson includes 'I can...' statements for self-assessment
The lesson uses the research principles: retrieval, spacing, interleaving, dual coding
The file naming follows a clear convention (e.g., sp_b1_15_review.html)
The lesson creates need for speaking (engagement hook) before presenting techniques
